title: Building the engine model, one verified layer at a time.
summary: The accepted Python foundation now connects to an observed nominal Rhino motion workflow, with a later synthetic port-geometry stage verified separately. Complete runtime persistence and physical engine validation remain distinct open gates.
revision: ENGINE SIMULATOR / SOFTWARE AND CAD EVIDENCE UPDATE
evidence: Accepted nominal software checks · physical validation pending
heroAlt: Accepted 19 October CAD motion correspondence distinguished from the later incomplete port workflow.
heroCaption: The 18 October Python gate, 19 October nominal CAD motion acceptance and 21 October synthetic port study are different milestones. Later port-workflow runtime acceptance remains incomplete.

sections.title: One foundation, several kinds of model
sections.text: The target is a digital twin of the entire engine. The Wahoo-owned, backend-independent Python foundation covers nominal motion, geometry and evidence handling; it does not replace a combustion or engine-performance solver. Actual copied-geometry motion correspondence was accepted on 19 October. Later port construction is a separate workflow whose full runtime gate remains incomplete in the reviewed 21 October records.

figure.alt: Frozen Python motion connected to actual Rhino document observations and independent comparison.
figure.caption: Updated 21 October review: actual nominal motion correspondence was accepted on 19 October. This is software/CAD evidence, not a coupled physical twin.

sections.title: Start with motion we can trace
sections.text: The historical motion model uses nominal rigid bodies, zero cylinder offset and constant angular speed. The graph reuses all 361 original one-degree samples. It shows piston travel and signed velocity, with no fitted or smoothed curve. The 12,000 rpm source reference is a design example, not a safe operating limit or a measured engine run.

figure.alt: Two plots of piston travel in millimetres and signed piston velocity in metres per second against crank angle from 0 to 360 degrees.
figure.caption: Frozen historical samples, reproduced unchanged as connected points. Travel and velocity are positive toward the crankshaft. Nominal dimensions and actual mechanical interfaces remain unverified.

sections.title: The original 18 October Python gate
sections.text: On 18 October, 21 admission checks passed. The final suite recorded 542 passes, no failures and one Rhino integration check not run. It covered historical motion, 54 parameter combinations, derivative convergence, cold-volume semantics, units and frames, invalid inputs and reproducibility. Two test-recording defects were repaired while retaining failed attempts; equations and acceptance thresholds were not relaxed.

figure.alt: Eight software-check categories total 542 passes, with Rhino A6 separately labelled not run.
figure.caption: Historical 18 October final-suite counts, retained unchanged. Rhino was not run in that suite; the later 19 October actual CAD gate is a separate acceptance record.

sections.title: Keep the earlier solver roadmap in view
sections.text: The earlier roadmap investigated a Wahoo interface around licensed EngMod2T. Static documentation and example-file review supported further investigation; they did not demonstrate a Wahoo performance run or vendor integration. Internal-stinger modelling still needs mapping to Wahoo’s straight exhaust. Port/scavenging assumptions and the annular-rim piston representation require review. Trial activation and unattended integration are not established by the Python gate.

sections.title: Preserve the foundation as it moves
sections.text: An accepted 18 October migration established a dedicated simulator home, explicit local execution and verified synchronization. The same nominal regression passed again: 542 passes, no failures, with Rhino not run in that migration check. Separately, 39 storage checks passed and 245 inventoried originals remained unchanged. The later 19 October CAD connection does not rewrite this earlier software/storage evidence.

sections.title: A pass at one layer is not a pass at every layer
sections.text: The 19 October gate accepted nominal copied-piston motion, saved/reopened correspondence and rejected-update/rollback checks. It did not validate physical geometry or installed fit. A later port workflow observed motion but stopped at persistence/evidence-identity gates. Qualified offline corrections are useful component evidence; they do not retroactively pass the failed runtime or establish complete later integration.

figure.alt: Observed later motion and offline persistence repairs separated from incomplete full runtime acceptance.
figure.caption: Latest reviewed offline serialization gate, 21 October: 154 component checks passed; a fresh runtime producer and complete external gate remain undemonstrated.

sections.title: A separate synthetic port-geometry milestone
sections.text: On 21 October, 40 synthetic fixture groups and 542 applicable frozen checks passed before an authorized two-family, 18-context timing/opening screen. It supports reproducible cold geometric reasoning. It does not predict pressure, power, safe engine speed or manufacturing suitability. The separate investigations explain the actual CAD connection and synthetic timing study in more detail.

sections.title: The next useful comparisons
sections.text: Future engine/exhaust comparisons should use source-qualified inputs, packaging and propulsion-load constraints, conservation and convergence checks, and sensitivity to uncertain inputs. Complete ECU behaviour, coolant flow and detailed metal temperatures need their own models and measurements; prescribed inputs cannot substitute for them. Bench and dyno evidence must eventually calibrate and challenge predictions. These are development requirements, not completed simulations.
